paras: The killing of Jordan Thompson was the shooting of a Black man by a pursuing party near Dresden, Tennessee, after he was accused of cutting a white man on Sunday, July 31, 1881. According to the widely reprinted Dresden dispatch, officers shot him dead when he refused to surrender, while one Pennsylvania digest attributed the killing to "the avengers of Prewett." Northern and Southern papers carried the news as a brief crime item over the following week.

A dispatch from Union City described Thompson as the brother of Joe Thomson, who was said to have shot Constable Henry Cowardine the previous week while Cowardine was trying to arrest him. No other report of that shooting appears in the coverage.

On Sunday, July 31, Thompson, described as "colored," was accused of cutting a white man with a razor at Dresden and then fleeing. The Union City dispatch and a Maine brief named the white man as Prewett, or Pewett, and said Thompson had cut his throat; none of the reports gave his condition. Thompson was pursued, and when he refused to surrender he was shot dead. The Union City account said he was "riddled with buckshot, killing him instantly."
No shooter was named, and no report of an inquest or of any arrest appears in the coverage.

The story reached most papers as a two-sentence Associated Press-style dispatch datelined Dresden, August 2, which the Richmond Dispatch, New-York Tribune, Savannah Morning News, Austin Weekly Democratic Statesman and both Dallas Heralds printed nearly word for word. Headlines cast Thompson as the offender: "An Escaping Criminal Shot Dead" in Richmond, "Killed His Man and Gets Killed" in Dallas, and "A Razor Slasher Shot" in the Somerset Herald on August 10. The Alexandria Gazette ran the fuller Union City version under "A Murderer Killed," and the Wilmington Daily Republican summarized it as a death "while resisting arrest for a murderous assault."

Several papers printed the item beside the Dyersburg lynching of Mike Walls, reported the same day. The Lancaster Intelligencer placed Thompson in a wry "How They Met Death" digest next to a drowning and a dog killed at a duel, the only report to call the killers "avengers."

The reports differ on who killed Thompson: the Dresden dispatch said officers, the Lancaster digest said "the avengers of Prewett," and the Union City dispatch did not identify the pursuers. The Lancaster digest also placed the killing "at Union City," apparently following the dateline of the Union City dispatch, which itself located the cutting at Dresden. The Kennebec Journal dated the cutting "yesterday" rather than Sunday.

reader.title: Killing of Jordan Thompson
bases: Thompson was killed by a pursuing party (officers in the Dresden dispatch, 'the avengers of Prewett' in one digest) after he fled an alleged cutting and refused to surrender (A1, A2, A3).

Thompson was shot dead in pursuit over an alleged cutting (A1, A3), but the main dispatch says officers shot him when he refused to surrender (A3), while only a digest calls the killers 'avengers of Prewett' (A2); no report gives their number or shows that they acted outside the law.

Two separately datelined dispatches, from Dresden (A3) and Union City (A1), agree that Thompson, accused of cutting a white man, was pursued and killed after refusing to surrender; A4 and A5 carry condensed versions.

accounts.label: Dresden AP dispatch
accounts.gist: On Sunday Thompson cut a white man with a razor and fled; officers pursued him and shot him dead when he refused to surrender.

accounts.label: Union City dispatch
accounts.gist: Thompson, brother of a man who had shot a constable the week before, cut the throat of a white man named Prewett at Dresden on Sunday; pursued, he refused to surrender and was 'riddled with buckshot'. The pursuers are not identified.

accounts.label: Lancaster digest
accounts.gist: Thompson was killed at Union City, 'riddled with buckshot by the avengers of Prewett'.

framing.detail: The Dresden dispatch ran nearly word for word from Richmond to Dallas, under headlines treating Thompson as a criminal ('An Escaping Criminal Shot Dead', 'Killed His Man and Gets Killed', 'A Razor Slasher Shot').
The Alexandria Gazette headed the Union City version 'A Murderer Killed' and tied Thompson to a brother who had shot a constable.
The Lancaster Intelligencer listed the death in a wry 'How They Met Death' digest, calling the killers 'the avengers of Prewett'.

conflicts.note: The Dresden wire dispatch, the most widely reprinted, names officers; the Lancaster item is a digest whose source is not shown.
